---
title: "Why sweep?"
---

## Sensitivity to hyperparameters

The quality of a model depends on its training data, learning algorithm and
*hyperparameters*: settings such as learning rate and network width. Models can
be sensitive to these settings, so *sweeping* or *tuning* them can substantially
improve performance.

Large neural networks can memorise their training data. We therefore need
held-out data to assess how well a model generalises. METIS partitions a
simulation bank into training, validation and test sets **by parameter group**,
keeping all realisations of a SIRDS parameter setting together. Fit the model on
training data, choose hyperparameters using validation data, and use the test
set for the final evaluation.

## Basic sweeping

The basic hyperparameter sweep workflow is:

1. Choose hyperparameters to fix (e.g. batch size) and sweep over (e.g. learning rate).
2. Choose the validation metric to target.
3. Choose how to sample the sweep space (e.g. random search or Bayesian optimisation) and how many training runs to make.
4. Launch one or more sweep agents.
5. Analyse the validation results and, if necessary, launch a more focused sweep.

When comparing different model families, use a common evaluation metric such
as RMSE in the original output units. Their training losses have different
meanings and cannot be compared directly.

The next two pages introduce [Weights & Biases](wandb.qmd) and walk through a
[sweep on SIRDS](sweep-config.qmd). For a small local grid, Hydra's
[`--multirun`](../basics/hydra.qmd) also works without W&B.
